findings.message: Migration 0007 adds two personal-data tables, but neither has a retention entry. `time.reminder` stores `user_id`, `sent_by` (a `*_by` column), `sender_name` (a name column with no id beside it) and the sender's free-text `message`. `time.project_reminder` stores `updated_by`. Requests, holds and erasure find rows only through `subject` and `subjectName`, so they never reach these rows. Add an entry for `time.reminder` with subject ["user_id","sent_by"], subjectName ["sender_name"] and fields ["message","sent_by","sender_name"]. Add an entry for `time.project_reminder` with subject and fields ["updated_by"].
findings.scenario: Erase Maya Fernando → time.reminder rows still hold sender_name='Maya Fernando' and sent_by='user:<maya>', and Team time keeps showing 'Reminded … by Maya Fernando'.

findings.message: `onProjects` reads the allocations and HR schemas directly with raw SQL (`allocations.allocation a join hr.person p`). architecture.md says cross-module reads go through the owning module's contract functions, which apply the caller's data scope. This read skips the boundary and the scope, and `check:graph` can't see it because no import is involved. `expectedBy`/`expectedIn` feed Team time, reminders, utilisation and Not started. Read allocations through `@amax/allocations/contracts` and persons through `@amax/hr/contracts`, as capacity.ts already does.
findings.scenario: A PM scoped to one entity → `onProjects` reads every allocation and every hr.person in the tenant, regardless of what Allocations' contract would let that PM see.

findings.message: `claimChoice` claims the other options' keys as cancelled, but it never checks that this option is still pending, and it doesn't claim this option's own key under the lock. When two options are confirmed at once, each can cancel the other: A commits its claim on B; B then takes the lock, still sees A in pending, claims A's key as cancelled and settles it. Both runs then hit CancelledByKeyError. The person confirmed an option and is told it was cancelled. The race test only asserts `ran.length <= 1`, so it stays green when nothing ran. Fix: under the lock, refuse when this action is already decided or its own key is claimed, and claim this option's key as in-flight before cancelling the others. Then assert exactly one write.
findings.scenario: Confirm option 1 and option 2 at the same moment (two tabs) → neither writes and both cards read 'Cancelled', although the person confirmed one.

findings.message: `claimKey(...).catch(() => ({ done: null }))` turns a failed claim, such as a DB error, into 'another option already ran'. `confirmCard` then records `not_chosen` and throws the cancelled outcome. A claim that could not be made must surface as an error or retry, never as a decision.
findings.scenario: A transient DB error while claiming a sibling key → the confirmed option is shown as 'Cancelled. Nothing was changed.' instead of an error the person can retry.

findings.message: Applying an 'add' request returns before the `mayMove` project check, and `add()` in decide-request.ts doesn't check the project either. `logEntry` with `requestId` also skips `assertCan`. A reviewer who is in the week's chain through project A can therefore log hours on project B, which they don't approve. On an approved week this is also a locked change. This is the same class as the earlier change-request project-scope lesson. Require `can(v, 'time:approve', { projectId })` for the proposed project, or the manager or Admin chain, in both the card and the service.
findings.scenario: Nimal (PM of Fleet Tracker only) reviews Kasun's submitted W42, which has Fleet Tracker hours. Kasun asks to add 3 h to HR Insights. Nimal applies it → HR Insights hours are logged without anyone who approves HR Insights.

findings.message: `remindNotStarted` wraps each person in `tx.transaction(...)` but never catches the error. One failure therefore aborts the whole remind_weeks service, including the weeks already reminded, instead of producing a 'failed' row. The week loop above catches per person; this second path doesn't. Wrap it in try/catch and push `{ status: 'failed', note: failureNote(e) }`.
findings.scenario: remind_weeks with 2 draft weeks and 1 Not-started person whose reminder insert fails → the whole card errors and nobody is reminded, instead of 'Reminded 2 · failed 1'.

findings.message: The new sent-back card shows a record (the rejected week, with who sent it back and why) but has no `PinButton`. Its Ask amax buttons carry a pin, but the card itself can't be pinned. Add `<PinButton inline pin={pin} />`.
findings.scenario: My timesheet for a rejected week → the 'Sent back' card has no + to pin it to chat.

findings.message: The new project-row pins name the project by name: `get_team_week {week, project: p.name}` here, and `get_timesheet {weekId, project: n}` in SheetPage.tsx. Both tools resolve by a case-insensitive name match, so a renamed project makes the pin resolve to null. 059 says a record is pinned by its UUID. Pass `projectId` and resolve by id.
findings.scenario: Pin Fleet Tracker on ThisWeek, then rename the project to 'Fleet Tracker v2' → the pin resolves to null and shows as unavailable.

findings.message: `markOf` marks the `?day=` day as 'missing' even after hours are logged for it, so the reminder link keeps a red Missing column on a filled day. Mark it only when `perDay` for that day is 0.
findings.scenario: Follow 'Log your hours for Fri Oct 23', log 8 h, reload → Friday still shows Missing in red.

findings.message: `dayRefusal` checks dates with `Date.parse`, which rolls an impossible date over (2026-02-30 becomes Mar 2). `workDay` in guards.ts rejects such dates with the `isoDate(d) !== day` check. Reuse that check so both copies agree.
findings.scenario: remind_missing {day:'2026-02-30'} → it passes the check and fails later as a raw DB date error instead of "isn't a real date".

findings.message: Row D6 of the Finance table is missing its closing `|`.

The new personal-data tables have no retention entries. `time.reminder` holds `sent_by`, `sender_name` (a name), `message` and `user_id`. `time.project_reminder` holds `updated_by`. module.ts `retention` gains no entry for either, which breaks the module standard (032): every personal-data table needs an entry with `subject` / `subjectName`. Erasure, legal holds and the purge never reach these rows. Fix: add entries. For `time.reminder`, use subject [user_id, sent_by] and subjectName [sender_name], with fields [message, sent_by, sender_name]. For `time.project_reminder`, use subject/fields [updated_by].
findings.scenario: An erasure request for Maya Fernando → her name stays in every `time.reminder.sender_name` row, and Team time keeps showing 'Reminded … by Maya Fernando'.

findings.message: The concurrent-confirm test asserts `ran.length <= 1`, so it passes when nothing is written. That outcome is reachable: A's `claimChoice` commits, then B's `claimChoice` claims A's key as cancelled before A's `withIdempotency` claims it. Both options end up cancelled. Assert exactly one write, or claim the chosen option's own key inside `claimChoice`'s transaction so a confirmed option can't be cancelled by a sibling afterwards.
findings.scenario: Two tabs confirm options A and B at the same moment → neither writes, and both cards say cancelled even though the person confirmed one.

findings.message: The README still says get_week_utilisation lists 'Only people with a timesheet that week'. `weekUtilisation` now also returns Not started people at 0 h. Update the doc line.
